flawed_step: The key step of the natural proof: "Since D has no short directed cycles, D has no directed cycles at all, so it has a source." This can't be justified. Ruling out cycles of length at most 3 does not rule out cycles of length 4 or 5 on 5 vertices. And if every vertex has in-degree at least 1, you can walk backwards along arcs and must eventually repeat a vertex, so the graph has a cycle. That cycle only has to be of length 4 or 5, which the hypothesis allows.
counterexample: The directed 5-cycle 1→2→3→4→5→1. It is loopless and its only directed cycle has length 5, so it has none of length at most 3. Every vertex has in-degree exactly 1, so no vertex has in-degree 0.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. A source is guaranteed only when the digraph has no directed cycles at all. Forbidding cycles of length at most 3 still allows a directed 4-cycle or 5-cycle, and the directed 5-cycle has no source. The proof breaks at the step from "no short cycles" to "no cycles".
